title: Asking with eikö ole with singular owners
summary: Ask negative possession questions with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä and fixed eikö … ole.
targetSkills: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions
objectives: Ask negative possession questions with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä and fixed eikö … ole.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: How the pattern works
paragraphs: Ask negative possession questions with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä and fixed eikö … ole.
Eikö is ei plus the question ending -kö. Put the owner between eikö and ole, then use the complete partitive noun: Eikö + owner + ole + thing.
keyPoints: Ask negative possession questions with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä and fixed eikö … ole.

steps: Add the question ending -kö to ei: ei + -kö = eikö. The neutral-only word ei takes the front-vowel ending.
minulla means “I as the owner”. Put this owner between eikö and ole.
Keep ole after the owner and the shown partitive palloa (“a ball”) last.
Eikö remains fixed with sinulla. Do not replace it with etkö from a personal-subject sentence.
sinulla means “you as the owner” for one person. Put this owner between eikö and ole.
Keep ole after the owner and the shown partitive kirjaa (“a book”) last.
Hänellä can mean “he” or “she”; either meaning uses the same eikö … ole frame.
hänellä means “he as the owner” or “she as the owner”; this example uses “she”. Put this owner between eikö and ole.
Keep ole after the owner and the shown partitive koiraa (“a dog”) last.
Changing the thing does not change the question word eikö.
minulla means “I as the owner”. Put this owner between eikö and ole.
Keep ole after the owner and the shown partitive kissaa (“a cat”) last.

examples.english: Doesn’t he or she have a car?
steps: hänellä identifies the singular owner in this asking with eikö ole with singular owners pattern.
Use Eikö + owner + ole; the negative question keeps this fixed verb pattern.
autoa (“a car”) is the complete regular singular partitive: auto + -a.
sinulla identifies the singular owner in this asking with eikö ole with singular owners pattern.
Use Eikö + owner + ole; the negative question keeps this fixed verb pattern.
peliä (“a game”) is the complete regular singular partitive: peli + -ä.

commonMistakes: Attach -kö to ei, not to ole: Eikö sinulla ole palloa? Keep ole as a separate word.
Use fixed eikö with minulla, sinulla and hänellä; keep ole after the owner.
Keep the shown partitive noun after the negative question pattern: palloa, rather than pallo.

optionFeedback.Eikö minulla ole kynää?: Ei + -kö gives eikö. Possession keeps eikö and ole unchanged for every owner; the noun uses its supplied partitive form.
optionFeedback.Eivätkö minulla ole kynää?: Ei + -kö gives eikö. Possession keeps eikö and ole unchanged for every owner; the noun uses its supplied partitive form. This choice uses the wrong verb form.
optionFeedback.Eikö minulla on kynää?: This choice changes the required polarity or leaves the required question pattern.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: eikö + possessor + fixed ole + singular partitive noun

parts.formation: Ei + the question ending -kö = eikö. The front-vowel ending follows ei, independently of the noun.

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Negative possession keeps ole after eikö, with every owner.
kynä + -ä = kynää. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed eikö ole in possession questions: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
